title: This portfolio website
desc: A static Next.js portfolio that deploys to GitHub Pages, works offline and runs on three runtime dependencies.
tech: Next.js, React, JavaScript, CSS, GitHub Actions, GitHub Pages, Service Worker
overview: A personal portfolio built as a static Next.js site: a home page, project pages with case studies, a Markdown blog, a command palette, a terminal, an English and Bangla switch and an offline-capable web app, all deployed to GitHub Pages.
problem: Show a developer's work on free static hosting with no backend, while keeping content easy to update and the site fast, accessible and honest about what it contains.
solution: Pre-render everything with Next.js static export, keep content in JSON files, generate SEO files and build facts in a prebuild step, and ship a small set of hand-written features instead of heavy dependencies.
decisions: Static export with no server: every page is pre-rendered HTML, so hosting is free and there is nothing to keep running.
Content lives in JSON files. Local browser editors validate and export it; publishing is a normal git commit and push.

Most features are written in-house instead of added as libraries: the Markdown renderer, syntax highlighter, command palette, terminal, charts and canvas effects. The project has three runtime dependencies (Next.js, React and React DOM).
Honest data: nothing on the site is invented. Sections with no real data simply stay hidden.
challenges: GitHub Pages has no server, so the sitemap, RSS feed and build facts are generated by scripts before the build.
The admin cannot write to the repository, so it validates, backs up and exports JSON instead of pretending to be a CMS.
Keeping links, assets and the service worker correct under a repository sub-path such as /portfolio/.
performance: Canvas effects pause when off-screen and switch off for visitors who prefer reduced motion.
Images are lazy-loaded with explicit dimensions to avoid layout shift.
The Under the hood section reports the page's real Core Web Vitals in the visitor's own browser.
security: Markdown is HTML-escaped and only https links and images are allowed.
Imported JSON is validated before it replaces a draft, and a backup is downloaded first.
No secrets in the client bundle, and no fake login: the admin pages are a local editor.
results: Deployable to free static hosting from a single GitHub Actions workflow.
Content updates need only a JSON edit and a push.
Designed to keep working offline once the service worker is active.
lessons: Separating data from presentation made every later feature (blog, project pages, CV, feed) cheap to add.
Pure logic is easy to test with small scripts; behaviour in a real browser still needs a real-browser pass.
audience: Visitors evaluating Abdul Kaium's work: employers, clients and collaborators.
requirements: Free static hosting with nothing to keep running
No invented data: sections without real data stay hidden
testing: Pure logic (content validators, Markdown renderer, profile generator, SEO file generation) is covered by Node's built-in test runner.
Browser behaviour has not been covered by an automated browser or accessibility suite yet.
deployment: A GitHub Actions workflow installs dependencies, validates content, runs tests, builds the static export and publishes it to GitHub Pages as a user site at the root domain. Pull requests are validated but never deployed.
limitations: No automated browser, accessibility or Lighthouse runs are recorded yet.
The admin editors are local tools: they cannot publish by themselves.
Visual effects were tuned by eye, not benchmarked.

nodes.name: Content files
nodes.desc: JSON and Markdown files in the repository: projects.json, posts.json, lib/profile.js and the decision records.
nodes.notes: Validated by scripts/validate-content.mjs before every build.

nodes.name: Browser editors
nodes.desc: Local pages under /admin/ that edit drafts in the browser and export validated JSON. They have no login and cannot write to the repository.
nodes.notes: Publishing is an export, a commit and a push.

nodes.name: Next.js static export
nodes.desc: Pre-renders the home page, project pages, article pages and the engineering page into plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in out/.
nodes.notes: Prebuild scripts also write the sitemap, RSS feed and build facts.

nodes.name: GitHub Actions
nodes.desc: Installs dependencies, validates content, runs tests, builds and uploads the Pages artifact.

nodes.name: GitHub Pages
nodes.desc: Serves the exported files from kaiumab10.github.io. There is no server and no database.

nodes.name: Visitor browser
nodes.desc: Runs the React UI and the in-house enhancements: command palette, terminal, language switch, filters and cursor effects.

nodes.name: Service worker
nodes.desc: Network-first cache with an offline fallback page, so the site can keep working without a connection after a first visit.
